title: Conditional Rendering

theory.english: Conditional rendering in React means showing different UI based on some condition. There are multiple patterns for this. The if/else statement works outside the return. The ternary operator works inside JSX for simple conditions. The logical AND operator (&&) renders something only when a condition is true. The optional chaining and nullish coalescing operators can also help with conditional rendering. Choosing the right pattern keeps your JSX clean and readable.
theory.hindi: React mein conditional rendering ka matlab hai ki alag-alag conditions ke basis par alag UI dikhana. Iske liye multiple patterns hain. if/else statement return ke bahar kaam karta hai. Ternary operator JSX ke andar simple conditions ke liye kaam karta hai. Logical AND operator (&&) tab kuch render karta hai jab condition true hoti hai.
theory.hinglish: Conditional rendering matlab alag-alag conditions par alag UI dikhana. if/else return ke bahar use karo. JSX ke andar ternary operator use karo. && operator tab render karta hai jab condition true ho. Sabse readable pattern choose karo apne case ke liye.

examples.title: Three Conditional Patterns
examples.explanation: Three patterns in one component: early return for blocking condition, ternary for either/or, and && for show/hide.

examples.title: Conditional CSS Classes
examples.explanation: Chained ternaries apply different CSS classes based on the type prop — a clean pattern for dynamic styling.

exercises.prompt: Create a component that shows a 'Loading...' text when an isLoading prop is true, and displays content when false.
exercises.expectedOutcome: Early return or ternary based on isLoading state.

exercises.prompt: Build a Score component that shows 'Pass' in green if score >= 60, or 'Fail' in red if below.
exercises.expectedOutcome: Ternary inside JSX applying different text and styles based on score.

quiz.question: Which operator renders JSX only when a condition is true (and nothing when false)?
quiz.explanation: The && operator only renders the right side when the left side is truthy. If false, it renders nothing.

quiz.question:
What does {count &&

Items

} render when count is 0?
quiz.explanation: When count is 0 (falsy), React renders the left value itself (0) which appears as text. Use count > 0 && ... to avoid this.

quiz.question: Which is the best approach to completely block rendering a component?
quiz.explanation: Returning null from a component tells React to render nothing for that component.

summary: Conditional Rendering chapter complete! Aapne teeno patterns seekhe — if/else, ternary operator, aur logical && operator.
